content:
You died, back in Hampstead's winding alleys, when the fog was engulfing the borough. And then you woke up. Wait, what?

You look at your hands - your skin seems paler, dark blood vessels making a striking contrast. You move - your muscle memory seems intact and you're not tripping over your own feet, though it hurts slightly more than you're used to.
But it's still you, you didn't get turned into some... chimera abomination by that mad scientist you've heard lives around. But then, what happened? And what will happen if anyone finds you...?
You stick to going out only in the fog, at first, staying in an abandoned building any other time. It's easy enough to hide there, and the pigeons are at least good companionship. But then the borough burns, and the fog fades, and reconstruction begins. You start to venture out during the night, to find something, anything, you can use as food - not that you need to eat, but chewing things helps you stay sane - but often, you come back to whatever shelter in the rubble you've managed to piece together to find it cleared away, and multiple times you've been disturbed from your rest - not sleep, never sleep - by people approaching, and have had to scramble to find a new place before anyone finds you.

Until one day, it all changes. You come back from a remarkably successful hunting expedition with a couple of lilac, juicy berries, to find - again - that your temporary shelter is mid-deconstruction. A quick look, and no one seems to be around besides a few pigeons; you allow yourself the luxury of a curse.
`Language!`
You look around, startled and fearful - but no one's there. You hear a slight giggling, though, and follow the sound to... one of the pigeons? Apparently mistaking your look of confusion for one of condemnation, the... pigeon? continues, `Yeah, yeah, I know I'm a hypocrite for that. Sorry, sorry.`
That's it. You've clearly lost what sanity remained. On a closer look, the pigeon has four wings - two of which are like a beetle's, three legs, horns... You pinch yourself, it hurts. So it's certainly not a dream, at least... though that means no chance of waking up from it. The pigeon is speaking again.
`So, uh, I guess you were sleeping here or something? Sorry about that, but you know we've got actual shelters set up, right?`
You didn't - but it's not like they'd accept you, anyway. So to save face, you mumble something about allergies. `Oh, we got some in the park without iron or silver if you need that. Or if it's a people allergy, we can find you some place to set up safely.`
This pigeon doesn't quit, do they...? They're peering at you closely, as if with recognition, before their eyes go wide. So this is where it ends.

`Hey, sorry if this is offensive at all. But, uh, you do know you're dead, right?`
...their question throws you off a bit, why would they apologise? Regardless, it won't change the outcome; you nod, and hold up the berries. 'Before you kill me, please... let me have one last meal, such as it were.'
`Oh, hey, that's where those berries I dropped got to.` ...they dropped these? `I'd ask why you think I'd kill you, but, uh... Been through that already. Trust me, I know. Well, second-hand---first-hand---one-and-a-half-hand? Dunno how it counts for me. My situation's a little complex.`
You stare in confusion as they shrug with both pairs of wings. `Long story. Just know you're not the first one I've Guided through this. Alright, so, from the sounds of it you've got no support at present, right? I'd get Sab to come talk to you, but she's officiating a wedding - who has weddings at dawn, anyway? And that's coming from someone who's awake then. But yeah. You got a few options...`
The pigeon starts rambling. A lot of the names they're spouting sound vaguely familiar, but you can't think where from... Their words seem to boil down to there being three places you can take shelter right now - the shelters in Hampstead or in 'Murry Hill', wherever that is, or... your ears prick up, did they just mention 'people like you'?

They seem to have picked up on your renewed interest. `Yeah, thought so. You're not the first Reborn they've taken in, and you won't be the last, either.  Alright, so - for the security of everyone who lives there, I can't take you straight to the Underfolk, but---`
'They're real? I thought they were just a legend, or a boogeyman to scare the children.'
`And that belief is exactly why we can't tell people where they live without a meeting. Thank you for coming to my birb talk.`
Though the pigeon's voice is serious, it also sounds kind - you get the feeling they're not scolding you, just stating a fact.
`So let's see. Most likely people to be able to set up a meeting at this hour are, hmm. You know where the cemetery is, and Murry Hill Park?` You know the first, but not the second, and tell the pigeon such. `Works out - I gotta get back to the park for a delivery, but I can delay a little bit to lead you there if needed, or you can just head to the cemetery.`
`If you wanna talk to someone as quick as possible, head to the cemetery, ask for Secel - she's the cute tiefling who took over recently - tell her Kukudh sent ya, and give her this note.` They pull some paper from their feathers, which has a scrawled, barely legible message - all you can make out is what looks like Infernal, and the signature `♡ Kukudh`.
`Alternative option - you can wait for Sab to be done with the wedding, I'll lead you back to the park. It'll take longer, but Sab's been in your situation before - I'm her Guide, that's how I know so much - so if you'd rather talk about it more first, there's your option.`

You think for a moment, and make your decision; the pigeon nods. `Got it. Don't you worry about a thing. And blessings of Sandigill on you or however Sab says it.`
Later that day, you're meeting with a representative of the Underfolk, and soon after, they've set you up with a shelter, with knowledge of how to adapt to your new life... with a family.
And weeks later, you run into the pigeon again, perching on the shoulder of a short Grung woman -  she smiles at you, a knowing smile, and the pigeon bows dramatically, saying just a few words as the two pass; `Seize the day, and stay determined, friend~`

Great. You're still stuck. Marv and Roman kept saying "don't worry, boss, we've got it, we can fix the car", but it's been half a day already. You got maybe two hours to the nearest town, and you'll get there before dusk only if you move soon. Which doesn't look likely. You shake your head and start thinking about making a camp for the night, and which of your employees are gonna be on watch. 

Frustrating.

Then a voice calls out to you from along the road.
"Hello there! Blessings of Sandigill to you. You seem to be having a bit of a trouble."

You look up. It's a man in a long coat, with long hair, and a wooden branching staff. Either a druid, or a weirdo. Or, possibly, a weird druid. Beside him, a short grung woman.
"Good evening" you reply. "Our engine's busted. We'll have to camp somewhere nearby."
"The town's not that far away. Let me have a look at that engine, you'll be back on the road in no time." the urban druid, for the lack of a better term, replies.
You can't help but raise an eyebrow. "Are you sure you know your way around engines?"
The man laughs heartily. "You're stuck anyway, what's the harm in trying?"

Before you can reply, he walks over to Marv and Roman, still bickering, and starts talking with them. You go a bit away for a quick smoke. They seem to be nodding to him, and let him to the engine. He does something weird with his staff and a wrench pops out of it. He gets to the engine.

You can see him doing some weird magic, and some... insects? Yeah, insects, coming out of his sleeves, forming into a hand, and moving into the engine. He waits a moment, talking with the woman in the meantime, and hits the engine with the wrench once. A bit of black liquid pours out, and into a bucket he quickly moved into place. He seems to be casting some other spell on it afterwards, and after a few quick taps, the engine whirrs back into life. Marv and Roman are nodding to one another, and you almost dropped the cigarette from your mouth.

"There you go, friend." the... druid? says. "Too much tension on on the transmission and it snaps. You should be good for two or three towns over, but the first parts shop you come across, get a replacement. Not much more I can do without access to parts out here."
"T-thanks. You really saved our skin." you muster.
"Don't mention it. Good luck to you on your way."
"Do you maybe need a ride there?" you ask.
"It's fine. We got all we need, and the night's still young. Great time for wandering."
You pause. "Okay, if you say so. We'll be on our way, then. Oh, actually. What's your name, good sir?"
"I'm Roy."

"Just a wandering mechanic."

All you wanted was a nice vacation.
You just wanted to take your partner and child to take a hike in the Wilds.
You didn't want to run into a bear. Particularly not one that's now chasing you---chasing your family---oh Silvanus, Epona, Cthulhu, whoever's out there, please save your family---

You trip over a branch. Your partner screams, but you call to them, 'Leave me! Keep going! Get away from here!'
As you struggle to your feet, you turn back to the bear, hoping to buy time for your family to escape. Your partner is hesitant, but for the sake of your child, they turn to flee towards a nearby shelter.
The bear reaches you, and you fight it as best as you can. It's no use.
You look to see your family one last time as you fade into unconsciousness. But it looks like they're... running back towards you?! No, that's... two other people...? You think?
Suddenly, a loud noise; the bear stumbles backwards. But it's too late. The last thing you see is a small bird zooming towards you from the direction of the pair.

You come to(?!) in a makeshift tent, a dull pain in your head along with everything else. A very strange imp floats before you. You manage to croak out, 'Is this Hell? I just wanted to protect my family... please, tell me they're safe.'
The imp laughs - you suppose it is an imp, after all, what did you expect. But as if summoned, an angel garbed in purple walks in---you blink a few times in surprise and your vision stabilises, it's just a short Grung woman holding a humanoid child. The woman speaks, 'How are you feeling? Your family is fine - they're at our shelter right now, but Kukudh will let them know you're awake.'
At that, the imp turns into a bird, and flies off. Your voice is hoarse, your thoughts confused, but you tell her about your pain, then ask, 'So... I'm not dead?'
She shakes her head. 'You're not. Your family encountered my husband and I in enough time that we were able to save you, though you'll likely have scars for life.' Seemingly absentmindedly, she rubs at a scar down the middle of her forehead. 'Consider it a reminder, I suppose.'
'But, the bear... did your husband kill it, then?' One of her eyes raises, and you feel... oddly scared. 'I-I mean, just, you don't look like the fighting t-type, you're so small, a-and---'
She stops you, and raises her robes to reveal gleaming mithral armour, and a holstered wooden revolver. 'Appearance isn't everything. I shot the bear, yes, but only to buy you time. My husband's been speaking with her to try and understand the situation.'

You can't help but look around in panic - the bear's here?! She tries to calm you down: 'Don't worry. She and her cub aren't intending to cause any harm, so long as you aren't. You're more alike than you think, you know.'
With that, a flap opens, and a bear---a smaller one?! There's two of them now?!---sticks its head into the room. You flinch in fear, but the Grung seems strangely unphased, even when the bear starts talking---wait, talking?!
'Hey, Sab, we got the situation figured out. She'd just like an apology from you for shooting at her, and our word that we'll act to prevent this happening again.'
The Grung - Sab? - nods, and pulls a lilac berry out of a pouch at her waist, bringing it over to you. 'Eat this, it'll help. Kukudh tells me your family will be here soon.' As you gladly take it, she leaves the tent, kissing the bear on the nose as she goes; it waits a moment, before seemingly judging (correctly) you'd be less nervous if it left and following her... 'Wait, is that bear her husband?'
`Yeah, what of it?` You didn't realise you spoke out loud, nor that the imp-pigeon-thing was back, your family in tow. You splutter for a moment in pure shock. 'I--- but--- he's twice her size---'
They laugh again, and grant you the mercy of finishing their sentence, `Roy's a shapeshifter, that's not his normal form. That expression on your face was great, though~`
As you blink rapidly, processing this information, the imp moves aside, and your partner and child rush into the tent to talk to you, and you're not sure if it's the pain, or the emotion, or the sheer weirdness of the situation, but you can't help but cry.

After a while, a loud noise shocks you out of your reunion. You struggle to your feet, worried about your saviours - it hurts, but far less than it really should... who ARE these people? No, that's something to worry about later, you think as you - supported by the surprisingly-strong imp and by your family - head to the tent flap to look outside.
You witness something you didn't expect. On one side, the she-bear which attacked you, a cub on her back. On the other - the smaller bear, the child, and the Grung woman. Both adult bears are digging a large hole; the woman seems to be commanding a hand made of water to move dirt aside.
As you watch, Sab nods, says something, and the bears step back; she makes a motion with her hands, and clean water begins to fill the pond, which the she-bear and cub drink from happily. The smaller bear, on the other hand, shimmers slightly as its---his---form changes into that of a humanoid man. A few bugs fly from his pocket to hand him a strange stone, which he starts to talk into. Nothing will surprise you any more, will it?

Sab notices you watching, smiles, and hops over. 'Alright, so... you went off the marked path, from the looks of it. Not too far off, not enough that it would be a problem under most circumstances, but you happened to run into her and her cub, who were also out of their normal roaming area due to a lack of water. Basically, she thought you were threatening her cub, and acted accordingly.'
'And then she... attacked us.' You can't help but sound a little bitter over that.
'Yes - to protect her cub. Wouldn't you do the same, fight to protect your family? Oh, yes, you did that.' She sounds a little stern, but reassuring. 'Anyway, that's where we came in. I shot in her general direction to draw attention, so that she would leave you alone, and Kukudh could get to you to stabilise you and channel my magic without getting killed themselves. I could bring you back from the dead in theory, but in practise, better to avoid that where possible - it's an exhausting process for everyone involved.'
...transforming? Channeling magic through an imp? Bringing people back from the dead?!
'My husband was then able to transform to talk to her, while I stayed to protect our child in the event of conflict. I'm glad it didn't come to it. We'd win, but I'd rather not fight if not necessary - especially when we understand her exact situation.'
She's so confident she could take on a bear, too... who are these people?
'Anyway, as you saw, we've made them a new pond. Roy's also talking with our friends at the City to hopefully raise awareness of keeping on the trail - they'd rather people stuck to the streets rather than go through their homes, why would wildlife be any different? As for you - you're free to go as soon as you feel better. Kukudh will stay with you until then, or fly back to the City to arrange transport. If you ever need anything, feel free to stop by Murry Hill.'

She's more perceptive than you thought... you weren't even aware your worry for your own fate was showing. 'I'm... thank you for being here, but... who are you...?' She smiles at your question.
'Just a wandering priestess of Sandigill, Warden of Waters. Your prayer to 'whoever's out there' reached him, you know - I got a sudden feeling we needed to go outside, and there you were.'
'...what can I---what can we do to repay you?'
'Respect life and nature, practise freedom and mercy. And do what you can with each day as it comes - you never know when it might be your last.' She bows, a little clumsily. 'Gil's blessings to you all.'

As she walks back to the man, you and your partner look at each other, and nod. You got a second chance at life today - it's time to put it to good use.

Sneak peak of work in progress:

*When the day finally comes for Rax and Jigsaw to make their final farewell, large crowds of fey gather round to give their well wishes…*
